standard_prerequisites.name: Purely inseparable elements as p-power roots
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 11080-11081
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies an element whose p^n-th power lies in k as purely inseparable over k in characteristic p.

standard_prerequisites.name: The p-power map in characteristic different from p
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that when the characteristic is not p the generator condition collapses to membership in k.

core_obligations: For a generator x in the first condition, split on the characteristic: if the characteristic is not p then the two conditions x^{p^n} in k and p^n x in k force x itself to lie in k (proof lines 11078-11079).
In characteristic p, the condition x^{p^n} in k says exactly that x is purely inseparable over k, which yields the second condition (proof lines 11080-11081).
proof_roadmap: Read the two equivalent conditions generator by generator, separating the case where the characteristic differs from p (proof lines 11077-11079).
In characteristic p, recognise the p-power condition as pure inseparability (proof lines 11080-11082).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives two equivalent descriptions of a field extension k' of k relative to a prime p: being generated by elements x with x^{p^n} in k and p^n x in k for some n, and being either equal to k or of characteristic p and purely inseparable over k (statement lines 11064-11075). The proof does not build a generator set for the second condition; it checks the first condition on a single arbitrary generator, splitting on the characteristic, where in characteristic different from p the condition p^n x in k kills the interesting case and in characteristic p the p-power condition is exactly pure inseparability (proof lines 11077-11082). The case distinction is the part that carries the content. H2.
